description: AES + block cipher modes decomposed. AES round structure, key schedule, AES-NI hardware acceleration. Modes: ECB (never), CBC (legacy), CTR (stream), GCM (authenticated), XTS (disk encryption). Why each mode exists and which to use.

sub_mechanisms.name: AES_round_structure
sub_mechanisms.definition: AES applies 10/12/14 rounds (128/192/256 key). Each round: SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey.
sub_mechanisms.why: SubBytes provides non-linearity; ShiftRows + MixColumns diffusion. 14 rounds for 256-bit ensures strong security margin. Reversible via inverse operations.

sub_mechanisms.name: AES_key_schedule
sub_mechanisms.definition: Derives N round keys from master key. Each round needs separate subkey.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same key reused across rounds would weaken security. Key schedule mixes original key + round constants. Standard part of AES spec.

sub_mechanisms.name: AES_NI_hardware
sub_mechanisms.definition: Intel/AMD instructions for AES rounds. aesenc, aesenclast, etc. 1 instruction per round.
sub_mechanisms.why: AES-NI: ~10 GB/s vs ~200 MB/s software. Standard on x86_64 since 2010. ARM has FEAT_AES. Universal modern AES is hardware-accelerated.

sub_mechanisms.name: ECB_mode_never_use
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each block encrypted independently with same key. Identical plaintext blocks → identical ciphertext blocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Famous penguin image: encrypted image preserves visible structure. Educational only. Should be disallowed by crypto libraries; some still expose for compatibility.

sub_mechanisms.name: CBC_mode_legacy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cipher Block Chaining. Each plaintext block XORed with previous ciphertext before encrypt. Requires IV.
sub_mechanisms.why: Sequential encryption (can't parallelise). Padding required. Vulnerable to padding oracle without proper MAC. Replaced by GCM in TLS 1.3.

sub_mechanisms.name: CTR_mode_stream
sub_mechanisms.definition: Counter Mode. AES encrypts counter values to produce keystream. XOR with plaintext.
sub_mechanisms.why: Parallelisable encryption + decryption. No padding. Foundation of GCM. CRITICAL: counter reuse with same key reveals plaintexts.

sub_mechanisms.name: GCM_authenticated_encryption
sub_mechanisms.definition: AES-CTR + GMAC. AEAD: confidentiality + integrity from one operation.
sub_mechanisms.why: TLS 1.3 mandates. Hardware-accelerated. Authenticates associated data (AD: headers) without encrypting. Standard modern mode.

sub_mechanisms.name: GMAC_construction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Polynomial MAC over ciphertext + AD using key-derived value. Defined in GF(2^128).
sub_mechanisms.why: Galois field MAC fast on hardware. Cost: nonce reuse breaks GMAC catastrophically (recovers authentication key). Nonce hygiene mandatory.

sub_mechanisms.name: XTS_disk_encryption
sub_mechanisms.definition: AES-XTS. Two-key mode designed for storage. Sector-aligned, no chaining between sectors.
sub_mechanisms.why: BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS use AES-XTS. Allows random access (no chaining). Cost: not authenticated (separate integrity layer needed).

sub_mechanisms.name: ChaCha20_alternative
sub_mechanisms.definition: Stream cipher. 20 rounds of ARX (Add-Rotate-XOR). No tables (constant-time by design).
sub_mechanisms.why: Fast on systems without AES-NI (ARM, mobile). Used in TLS 1.3, WireGuard, OpenSSH. Often paired with Poly1305 for AEAD.

sub_mechanisms.name: nonce_management
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each (key, nonce) pair must be unique. Strategies: random 96-bit nonces, counter, deterministic.
sub_mechanisms.why: GCM nonce reuse → catastrophe. Random 96-bit: 2^48 messages before collision risk. Counter: simple but state-dependent. Modern crypto APIs hide.

sub_mechanisms.name: padding_PKCS7
sub_mechanisms.definition: Padding scheme for block ciphers. Pad to block size with N bytes of value N.
sub_mechanisms.why: Required for CBC, not for CTR/GCM. Vulnerable to padding oracle without proper MAC. Modern: AEAD avoids the issue entirely.

derivation_rules.name: ECB_reveals_plaintext_patterns
derivation_rules.why: Same plaintext block → same ciphertext block. Structured data (images, regular records) becomes visually inspectable. Never use ECB.

derivation_rules.name: GCM_provides_integrity_naturally
then: any ciphertext modification is detected at decrypt
derivation_rules.why: GMAC over ciphertext fails on any change. Padding oracle attacks impossible. Modern AEAD approach to combined confidentiality + integrity.

derivation_rules.name: CTR_parallelism_at_random_access_cost
if: data is encrypted with CTR mode
derivation_rules.why: Each block depends only on counter, not previous blocks. CTR is parallelisable; CBC is sequential. Critical for high-throughput.

derivation_rules.name: nonce_reuse_GCM_catastrophic
if: GCM nonce repeated with same key
then: both plaintexts recoverable + authentication key leaks
derivation_rules.why: Both messages encrypt with same keystream → XOR reveals plaintexts. GMAC key derivable from nonce + tag. Disaster. Modern APIs prevent by generating nonces.

derivation_rules.name: AES_NI_makes_AES_GCM_universal_choice
then: AES-GCM is the fastest authenticated encryption
derivation_rules.why: ~10 GB/s with hardware support. Same hardware accelerates GMAC. ChaCha20-Poly1305 competitive only without AES-NI (mobile, embedded).
